title: Affinity-aware request dispatch and per-core local KV cache
author: Asha Patel
ci_status: pass (initial flaky failure in scheduler tests, rerun passed)
release_notes: Introduce an affinity-aware dispatcher and a core-local KV cache layer to reduce CPU-side tail latency and remove costly thread-affinity syscalls. Improves 99th percentile request latency under high concurrency. No API changes for end users; rollout via Canary by default.

description:
Context and motivation: We've observed recurring 99th percentile latency spikes under sustained multi-tenant load caused by CPU-side contention: global KV cache locks, excessive pthread_setaffinity calls from hot request handling paths, and work stealing that thrashes caches. This PR introduces two complementary approaches: (1) a CoreLocalKVCache that provides lockless fast-path reads and bounded global spill for writes/evictions; (2) an AffinityDispatcher that routes requests to worker groups with preferred CPU locality using a cooperative CpuHint API instead of forcing thread pinning.

Design summary: CoreLocalKVCache keeps a compact per-core shard index and a read-optimized ring backing. Reads consult the local shard first; misses fall back to a spill map protected by a thin mutex. Eviction is done by a background janitor per shard to avoid write-side stalls. The AffinityDispatcher maintains lightweight worker groups (N groups = sockets or vcpu groups) and assigns short-lived request tasks to a preferred group using per-worker run-queues and a cooperative CpuHint call that nudges the scheduler; we avoid repeated pthread_setaffinity to reduce syscall overhead and context churn.

Implementation highlights: 
- runtime/kvcache/core_local_cache.h/.cc: new implementation with lockless read path and small fixed-size per-core rings; public API matches existing KVCache interface so callers are unaffected.
- runtime/scheduler/affinity_dispatcher.*: new dispatcher with group registration and preferred-worker enqueue API.
- runtime/workerpool/cpu_hint.h: small abstraction that emits scheduler-friendly hints; on Linux this uses sched_yield + SOFT affinity heuristics, on other OSes it's a no-op behind a flag.
- tests/ and benchmarks/: microbenchmarks show improvements and integration tests validate fallbacks.

Benchmarks (pprof-style microbench, Linux x86_64, c6i.4xlarge): 
- baseline main (before change): p50=6.2ms p95=18.4ms p99=38.7ms throughput=2200 QPS
- this PR (canary): p50=5.9ms p95=12.1ms p99=21.3ms throughput=2300 QPS
Notes: gains come primarily from removing global lock stalls on KV reads and cutting ~0.5ms median from scheduling syscalls at high QPS.

Compatibility and rollout: API remains backward-compatible. Feature gated with --enable-cpu-hint and runtime config for enabling core-local cache. Default rollout plan: canary on 10% of requests for 24h, increase to 50% if no regressions, full rollout after 7 days.

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for local shard read/write semantics and an integration test exercising dispatcher failover. CI initially failed on a flaky scheduler unit test (timing-sensitive), flakiness fixed by relaxing a timing assertion and adding a retry harness. Final CI run passed.

Diff/changed areas (high-level): modified the scheduler and kvcache subsystems, added new tests and docs. Important new files: runtime/scheduler/affinity_dispatcher.cc, runtime/kvcache/core_local_cache.cc. Example hot-path snippet used in runtime: if (try_read_local(key, &val)) return val; // fast-path lockless read

Review and discussion: Reviewers asked for oversized-key fallback and gated platform tests; both addressed. Concern about cgroup scheduling semantics was discussed and documented. We decided not to expose the worker-group configuration to customers yet; it's an internal tuning knob.

Merge strategy and outcome: After addressing review comments and stabilizing tests, PR was squashed and merged into main on 2026-02-03 using squash merge. Release notes added.

Follow-ups and TODOs:
- ENG-6050: add telemetry to measure local-shard hit rates and record eviction pressure (linked linear).
- Explore adding a NUMA-aware worker group assignment when running on bare-metal with multiple sockets.
- Try a specialized lock-free hash for the spill map to reduce mutex contention under pathological workloads.

References: linear/ENG-5921, internal benchmarking doc: /docs/perf/affinity-dispatcher-bench.md, test plan in tests/integ/affinity_plan.md
